DILG • Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center. EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: l,'mvw. dilg.gov_ph 23 JUN 2016 DILG Legal Opinion No. 20 S. 2016 NITY. RITA LINDA V. JIMENO NITY. MICHAEL E. DAVID ATTY. ANDREA S. JOSON JIMENO COPE AND DAVID LAW OFFICES Counsel of Ms. Lydia J. Abrera 37th Floor Rufino Pacific Tower 6784 Ayala Avenue cor. V.A. Rufino Street Makati City Gentleman/Ladies: This has reference to your letter dated I I January 2016 seeking the Department's legal advice and request for a formal declaration on the validity of following documents: 1. 2. 3. Barangay Resolution No. 33, series of 2012 adopted by the Sangguniang Barangay of Barangay 194, Zone 20 on 05 August 2012 entitled "RESOLUTION APPROVING THE CONSTRUCTION OF MULTI-PURPOSE HALL TO BE USED AS MEAT SHOP LOCATED ALONG FOURTH STREET CORNER ROAD 7, THIS BARANGAY 194 ZONE 20"; Barangay Resolution No. 33-A, series of 2012 adopted by the Sangguniang Barangay of Barangay 194, Zone 20 on 16 August 2012 entitled "RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE BARANGAY CHAIRMAN TO NEGOTIATE AND ENTER INT CONTRACT WITH THE PRIVATE PARTY OFFERING TO BUILD A CONCRETE STRUCTURE (MULTI-PURPOSE HALL) PURPOSEDLY FOR A MEAT' SHOP LOCATED ALONG FOURTH STREET CORNER ROAD 7, AT NO COST FROM THE BARANGAY"; and Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) dated 22 January 2013 between Barangay 194 and Spouses Danilo B. Tario and Josie L. Tario. Per your letter, the above-enumerated documents were adopted and/or entered into during the term of Punong Barangay (P B) Felicisimo Arnesto. When Punong Barangay Lydia Abrera, your client, assumed office in 2013, she found several irregularities in the above-enumerated documents. Hence, on 26 September 2014, PB Abrera, together with Sangguniang Barangay Members Gilbert Gubisch, Ritasol dela Rosa and Ruben Campano filed before the Office of the Ombudsman a criminal

complaint for violation of Republic Act No. 3019 or the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act against PB Arnesto and the Sangguniang Barangay Members who served during his administration. Finding that the public officials involved occupied positions that are below Salary Grade 27, it was represented in your letter that the Office of the Ombudsman dismissed the case for lack of jurisdiction and referred the same to the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City for investigation. However, the Office of the City Prosecutor of Pasay City likewise dismissed the complaint for lack of jurisdiction, explaining that their office has no jurisdiction to determine the validity of the Barangay Resolutions and the MOA because the same is an administrative matter. As represented in your letter, the Office of the City Prosecutor advised that there must be a determination as to the validity of the Barangay Resolutions and the MOA with the proper office before they could determine the existence of probable cause to charge former Punong Barangay Arnesto and other Sangguniang Barangay Members for violation of RA 3019. Hence, your letter seeking legal advice and request for a formal declaration once and for all as to whether or not the above-enumerated documents are valid based on the following grounds: 1. 2. 3. 4. Former PB Arnesto had no authority to enter into an agreement with Sps. Tario as regards the construction of a "Multi-Purpose Hall" for the purpose of operating a meat shop since copies of Barangay Resolutions Nos. 33 and 33-A were never submitted, much less approved by the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Pasay City as mandated by RA No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 ; Barangay Resolutions Nos. 33 and 33-A were falsified since the Minutes of the Meeting dated IO August 2012 and 16 August 2012 did not include in its agenda any topic related to the construction of the Multi-Purpose Hall for the use of a meat shop and the authority to be granted to former PB Arnesto; The MOA was only an afterthought as it was executed on 22 January 2013, when Sps. Tario constructed the meat shop and began operating their business as early as the year 2012. As an evidence thereto, Mr. Bobby T. Arroyo executed an Affidavit confirming that indeed, former PB Arnesto caused the preparation of the Barangay Resolutions and MOA only in November 2013 to make it appear that the Sangguniang Barangay passed those resolution prior to the execution of the MOA; The MOA is grossly disadvantageous to the residents of Barangay 194 as the residents of Barangay 194 lost a place to hold wakes and funerals for their departed loved ones, thus forcing them to hold memorial services at the sidewalks, roads and alleys in front of their houses or to pay expensive funeral parlors to have a place to grieve;

5. The terms of the MOA are grossly disadvantageous to the barangay and the local government unit as the transaction is much like a build-operate-transfer (BOT) scheme whereby the Sps. Tario would be reimbursed for the expenses incurred in the construction of the building over a period of ten (IO) years by way of lease while they shall pay a monthly rent of Php4, 000 to the barangay. In this regard, please be informed that the Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government and as such, it has no authority to declare invalid any ordinance or resolution of the local sanggunians, or any act committed by the members thereof which is alleged to be in violation of the Republic Act No. 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991 (hereinafter, "the Code) or other applicable laws. Only the courts have the authority to do so upon initiation of appropriate action/s such as a petition for declaration of nullity of the resolution. The same is true with regard to your allegation of legal infirmity of the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) entered into by Barangay 194 with Sps. Tario. For this, we shall discuss only the provisions of law or rules which we deem applicable based on your representations in your letter. l. As to the scope of the review power of the Sangguniang Panlungsod over legislative measures enacted by the Sagguniang Barangay, Section 57 (a) of the Code is instructive, thus: Section 57. Review of Barangay Ordinances by the Sangguniang Panlungsod or Sangguniang Bayan. — (a) Within ten (IO) days after its enactment, the sangguniang barangay shall furnish copies of all barangay ordinances to the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan concerned for review as to whether the ordinance is consistent with law and city or municipal ordinances. (b) If the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan, as the case may be, fails to take action on barangay ordinances within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof, the same shall be deemed approved. (c) If the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan, as the case may be, finds the barangay ordinances inconsistent with law or city or municipal ordinances, the sanggunian concerned shall, within thirty (30) days from receipt thereof, return the same with its comments and recommendations to the sangguniang barangay concerned for adjustment, amendment, or modification; in which case, the effectivity of the barangay ordinance is suspended until such time as the revision called for is effected. (Emphasis Supplied)

Based on the aforequoted provision, only barangay ordinances are to be submitted to the sangguniang panlungsod for review. With respect to resolutions passed by the sangguniang barangay, the same need not be submitted to the sangguniang panlungsod for review l. Jurisprudence is replete of' cases enumerating the differences of an ordinance from a resolution, viz: 2. LIIs/17 We are not convinced by petitioners insistence that the terms resolution and ordinance are synonymous. A municipal ordinance is different from a resolution. An ordinance is a law, but a resolution is merely a declaration of the sentiment or opinion of a lawmaking body on a specific matter. An ordinance possesses a general and permanent character, but a resolution is temporary in nature. Additionally, the two are enacted differently a third reading is necessary for an ordinance, but not for a resolution, unless decided otherwise by a majority of all the Sanggunian members?. As to the necessity of sanggunian resolution before the Punong Barangay may enter into a contract in behalf of the barangay, Section 22 of the Code is instructive, thus: Section 22. Corporate powers---xxx (c) Unless otherwise provided in this Code, no contract may be entered into by the local chief executive in behalf of the local government unit without prior authorization by the sanggunian concerned. A legible copy of such contract shall be posted at a conspicuous place in the provincial capitol or the city, municipal or barangay hall. (Emphasis Supplied) The foregoing is also reiterated in Section 391 (a)(12) of the Code. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Ve ruly yours, AUS REA. P ERO Copmrnished: DIR. MA.
